title: Commutes Sentence of Robert Francis
description_medium: On January 19, 2021, President Donald Trump commuted Robert Francis’s federal sentence, according to the Justice Department’s clemency list. The department identifies his Eastern District of Missouri case and says he had been sentenced to life in prison plus five years of supervised release for conspiring to distribute and possessing cocaine. The listing records the sentence before the commutation; it does not state the replacement terms or explain why Francis was selected.
description_long: The Justice Department’s Office of the Pardon Attorney lists Robert Francis among the people whose sentences President Donald Trump commuted on January 19, 2021. The entry identifies an Eastern District of Missouri case in which Francis was sentenced on October 3, 2002, to life imprisonment and five years of supervised release. The listed conviction was conspiracy to distribute cocaine and possession with intent to distribute cocaine. These details establish the punishment and federal offenses recorded before the clemency action, but the public table does not spell out how much of the sentence Francis had served or what new sentence Trump imposed. A commutation changes a sentence; it does not erase the conviction. The listing also gives no case-specific explanation for the decision, so it supports documenting the action and its context, not a claim about motive or favoritism. The public disclosure column links to clemency records, which may provide more detail than the summary table.
